mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates strong economic growth, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 9% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If unemployment exceeds 9% but S&P 500 returns remain positive.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment increases and employment decreases, it indicates a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If both unemployment rises and employment falls but S&P 500 returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, higher federal funds rates increase borrowing costs, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If federal funds rate exceeds 4% but S&P 500 returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in industrial production indicates increased economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If industrial production grows but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in CPI suggests inflationary pressures, which can negatively impact S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If CPI exceeds 230 but S&P 500 returns remain positive.

mechanism_narrative: Increased housing starts and retail sales signal strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If both housing starts and retail sales increase but S&P 500 returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, slowing GDP growth may lead to negative S&P 500 returns as growth peaks.
failure_condition: If GDP growth slows but S&P 500 returns remain positive.
